question: Why was the Cyrene-based separation of cathode scraps run at room temperature?
rendered: The document does not mention running the Cyrene-based separation of cathode scraps at room temperature. In fact, it mentions that the separation process should be kept above 90 °C, as the PVDF binder dissolved in Cyrene at that temperature. The process was actually run at 100 °C to successfully reclaim the cathode materials while avoiding the re-precipitation of PVDF.
